items.text: Amid World War II, Central Utah Vocational School (CUVS) was established to provide essential war production training.
The institution expanded its commitment to career-focused and technical education.
Willy the Wolverine, named after President Sorensen, became the school’s mascot in the 1967–68 school year.
The UVU Rodeo team started, paving the way for future programs.
Utah Technical College at Provo moved to primarily offer classes at the university’s current Orem Campus location.
Utah Technical College became Utah Valley Community College (UVCC).
The institution became Utah Valley State College (UVSC), now offering four-year degrees.
The first classes took place in the current Wasatch Campus.
On July 1, Utah Valley University (UVU) was officially born.
The Ira A. and Mary Lou Fulton Library officially opened on July 1.
The Capitol Reef Field Station began operations on Oct. 16.
The Green Man group was formed.
The Military-Affiliated Student Hub (MASH) began serving military-connected students.
President Astrid S. Tuminez began her tenure, focusing on innovation, inclusion, and growth.
The state-of-the-art Noorda Center for the Performing Arts opened, quickly becoming a cultural hub in Utah County.
The UVU Pedestrian Bridge, the largest such bridge in the state, was unveiled, connecting UVU to the UTA FrontRunner Orem Central Station.
UVU expanded its reach by opening a campus in Lehi, an extension of the College of Health and Public Service.
